figures.paper: !2024-Nature-Detecting hallucinations in large language models using semantic entropy_SI&Highlights.pdf
figures.caption_text:
Fig. 3 | Detecting GPT-4 confabulations in paragraph-length biographies. 
The discrete variant of our semantic entropy estimator outperforms baselines 
both when measured by AUROC and AURAC metrics (scored on the y-axis). The 
AUROC and AURAC are substantially higher than for both baselines. At above 
80% of questions being answered, semantic entropy has the highest accuracy. 
Only when the top 20% of answers judged most likely to be confabulations are 
rejected does the answer accuracy on the remainder for the P(True) baseline 
exceed semantic entropy.

figures.paper: 2026-Nature-Reimagining research papers as interactive and reliable AI agents_Briefing&SI.pdf
figures.caption_text:
Figure 1 | Moving from research paper to interactive AI agent.  Paper2Agent analyses a paper and 
its codebase to build a remote model context protocol (MCP) server (a standardized interface through 
which artificial-intelligence systems use software). This is done through Paper2MCP, which is the 
first step of Paper2Agent. The server creates or identifies tools (executable functions that implement 
the paper’s methods, indicated here by Tool 1 and Tool K), resources (the manuscript, data and 
supplements) and prompts (step-by-step workflows for analysis). Connecting a large language model 
(LLM) to the MCP, through a platform such as Hugging Face, creates a paper-specific agent that can 
answer questions, reproduce analyses and apply the methods to fresh data through natural-language 
requests. Miao, J. et al./Nature (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0).
